transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have an international airline interested in licensing the independent concert documentary for their passenger-entertainment system. Their draft package proposes a worldwide, twelve-month, non-exclusive license using the current picture and delivery master. Before I can sign off on the final license terms and delivery instructions, I need our rights, music, and post-production leads to report any approval conditions. Let's start with rights -- are there any clearance issues we need to flag?

transcript.text: I reviewed the executed performer agreements yesterday and confirmed that the documentary may be licensed only in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom for a six-month non-exclusive term. The agreements also require a written rights amendment before delivery. The buyer's draft arrived after I completed that review, so we need to flag that the proposed worldwide, twelve-month scope exceeds what we're currently cleared for.

I completed the airline's ingest test with the delivery vendor today and confirmed that their required master is 1080p SDR video with stereo Lt/Rt audio and English SDH captions delivered as a sidecar VTT file. Our current master is 4K with a different audio and caption package, so it does not meet the airline's ingest spec. I have not yet issued the revised export order because the licensing terms are still pending — but we'll need a new export to satisfy delivery requirements.
